source.title: Disagreement and returns: The case of cryptocurrencies

hypothesis: A focal-asset abnormal-volume spike proxies disagreement/overpricing and predicts lower next-day crypto returns; therefore a market-neutral long-low-abnormal-volume / short-high-abnormal-volume portfolio should earn positive next-day net returns.
universe: Point-in-time Binance USD-M USDT perpetuals. Each UTC day retain the top 50 contracts by lagged trailing-30-day quote volume among assets with exact daily history and valid abnormal-volume statistics.
feature: DISAGREE proxy = (yesterday quote volume - mean of the preceding W completed daily quote volumes) / std of those W volumes. Signal is negative DISAGREE so higher signal means lower abnormal volume.
portfolio: Equal-weight long lowest-abnormal-volume quintile / short highest-abnormal-volume quintile, 0.5 gross per side.
execution: At UTC day d open use volume data only through d-1; hold to next UTC day open. No same-bar fill.
development_gate: Canonical mean rank IC of -DISAGREE >0.02 with HAC p<0.05; positive low-minus-high abnormal-volume return spread; canonical net daily Sharpe >0.70 and total return >0; at least 3/4 windows positive after base costs.
success_gate: Canonical OOS net Sharpe >1.0; OOS IC >0.02; positive total return at 2x costs; at least 3/4 windows positive; 2024 and 2025 non-negative; max drawdown <35%; excluding BTC/ETH positive; excluding strongest contributor positive; one-day delayed implementation positive; DSR reported.
source_deviation: The source uses spot-market turnover and finds the effect strongest under short-sale constraints. This test uses quote-volume abnormality on perpetuals because market capitalization/turnover denominator is unavailable. The perps setting may weaken the source mechanism; that limitation is fixed before results.
